Sportsbook Odds / College Football Odds


College Football Odds – NCAA Football Spreads, Moneylines and Totals

Stay on top of the latest 2026–2027 College Football odds with FanDuel Sportsbook - your trusted source for real-time lines across every NCAA conference, from the SEC and Big Ten to the Sun Belt, MAC, and beyond. Whether you’re betting regular season rivalries or postseason bowl games, FanDuel offers accurate, expert-driven college football odds across spreads, totals, moneylines, and futures.

As an legal sportsbook for college football, FanDuel delivers data-powered lines, lightning-fast updates, and flexible wagering tools that let you track line movement, capitalize on live betting windows, and combine bets for boosted payouts.

Popular College Football Betting Markets

At FanDuel, you can bet on NCAA Football in ways that suit your strategy and level of experience. Here are the most popular College Football bet types we offer:

College Football Point Spreads: Bet on a team to cover the spread, not just win. Favorites must win by more than the spread; underdogs can win outright or lose within the margin. For example: Alabama -7.5 vs. Texas means Alabama must win by 8+ for your bet to cash.


College Football Moneylines: Pick the outright winner of the game with no spreads involved. Favorites are denoted with a minus (-) and underdogs with a plus (+). For example: Michigan -190 means you mus wager $190 to win $100. Likewise, Clemson +150 means a $100 bet pays $150 if they win.


College Football Over/Under Totals: Wager on the total combined points scored by both teams. You can also bet 1st half, 2nd half, or individual quarters. If the Over/Under is set at 37.5: a 21-17 final score (38 combined points) hits the Over, while a 24-13 score (37 combined points) hits the Under.


Live College Football Odds: Bet in real-time as the game unfolds. FanDuel adjusts live odds between drives, during timeouts, and after major plays like turnovers or touchdowns.


Parlays and Same Game Parlays: Link multiple bets - like spread + total or first-quarter lead + full-game win—into one ticket for a higher payout. All legs must win to cash.




How to Read College Football Odds

College football odds are shown in American moneyline format:

Spreads: A minus sign (–) shows the favorite and the number of points they are favored. A plus sign (+) shows the underdog.
Moneylines: –150 = Bet $150 to win $100 (favorite). +180 = Bet $100 to win $180 (underdog)
Totals: If Over/Under is set at 58.5 and the final score is 31–28 (59 total), the Over wins.

Odds can also result in a push (tie) when the margin hits exactly—such as a 3-point win on a -3 spread.



Why FanDuel is Trusted for College Football Betting


Expert-Set Lines powered by real-time injury updates, betting splits, and player-level analytics
Official Data Feeds from NCAA football broadcasts and analytics providers
Flexible Markets: From player props to live Same Game Parlays and game props.
Safe and Legal: Licensed in all operational U.S. states with responsible gaming tools such as deposit limits, timeouts, and support always available.


How to Bet on College Football with FanDuel


Log in or download the FanDuel Sportsbook app
Navigate to NCAAF odds via the menu
Browse lines, add bets to your slip, and confirm your wager

You can track all bets live within the app, monitor cash-out options, and manage your bankroll with intuitive controls.

For a broader overview, see our complete College Football betting guide.



College Football Odds and Betting FAQs


Do overtime periods count for my college football bets?

Yes - overtime counts for all markets unless stated otherwise. Second-half markets (revised at halftime) also include overtime. Note that fourth-quarter specific markets do not include overtime.

What has to happen for player props to have action?

For college football, an offensive player must play at least one offensive snap and a defensive player at least one defensive snap for proposition bets to stand. Touchdown scorer bets require the player to play at least one snap. More generally, player prop selections are void only when the player does not play a snap in the game.

Do quarter/half markets include overtime?

For quarter/half bets, the entire period must be played for action. Second-half markets include OT; fourth-quarter markets do not include OT.

How much of the game must be played for bets to stand? What if the game is suspended or postponed?

Under American Football general rules (which cover college football unless a specific override applies): At least 10 minutes of official time in the 4th quarter must elapse for bets to have action. If the game starts but is suspended before that threshold and not completed within 24 hours, unsettled bets are void. Abandoned/postponed games must be resumed within 60 hours of initial kickoff for action (otherwise void).

How are Same Game Parlays (SGPs) handled if one leg is void?

If any leg in a parlay is void (e.g., a selection is a non-runner/void), FanDuel adjusts the parlay accordingly (e.g., a treble becomes a double). Same Game Parlays are settled the same way.
